title: Why Mics Scream: Feedback Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 12
description:
Aarav walks near the speaker with a microphone and the hall fills with a scream. He steps back and it stops. The sound looped back into the microphone: that loop is feedback. We start with two everyday pictures: steering a drifting bicycle back (negative feedback) and a cheering crowd that keeps getting louder (positive feedback).

On a live breadboard an amplifier with gain A gets a feedback network of two resistors (feedback ratio beta) and a mixer. With negative feedback the output on the oscilloscope gets smaller but stays clean; flip to positive feedback and it grows, hits the supply limits and keeps going with no input at all. Then we derive the gain with feedback A_f = A/(1 + A beta) and A/(1 - A beta), see why A beta = 1 makes an oscillator, compare uses, and work an example with both kinds. Then the exam trap (negative feedback has 1 + A beta, and this beta is not the transistor's current gain), where it is asked, an original practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 71 of PUC Electronics, Class 12, Chapter 4: Feedback in Amplifiers (Karnataka II PUC Electronics). Feedback amplifiers are not in the rationalised NCERT/CBSE Class 12 Physics book or the current ISC Physics syllabus, so this lesson follows the Karnataka PUC Electronics syllabus.
